name: Anterior approach to C1–C2
corridor: Transverse cut, platysma, fascia along the anteromedial sternocleidomastoid border, blunt plane between carotid sheath and trachea/esophagus to prevertebral fascia at C1–C2

positioning.text: Position so a nasogastric tube and the endotracheal tube can be felt and C1–C2 can be imaged.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the sternocleidomastoid and midline viscera. Left-sided approaches make the recurrent laryngeal nerve more predictable; right-sided approaches let it be seen and protected.

incision.text: Make a transverse cut at the required high cervical level for a better scar.

superficial_interval.text: Divide platysma in line with the skin, then divide deep cervical fascia along the anteromedial sternocleidomastoid border.

deep_interval.text: Bluntly develop the plane between the carotid sheath and the trachea/esophagus to prevertebral fascia. Open that fascia longitudinally, confirm the level, mobilize longus colli, and place distractors. Identify and protect the recurrent laryngeal nerve. A nasogastric tube marks the esophagus.

layers.text: Skin, platysma, deep cervical fascia, carotid-sheath versus visceral plane, prevertebral fascia, longus colli, then C1–C2.

structures_at_risk.text: The esophagus, recurrent laryngeal nerve, and carotid artery are at risk. Esophageal injury is potentially lethal.

danger_zones.text: Sharp dissection through the carotid sheath or viscera, and working without a nasogastric tube to mark the esophagus, are the danger zones. Hold carotid bleeding with direct pressure and call vascular surgery.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not retract forcefully on the esophagus or carotid sheath.

exposure.text: Shows the anterior C1–C2 bodies through the same interval as a subaxial anterior cervical approach, placed more cranially.

limitations.text: This is not a transoral window and does not replace posterior C1–C2 fixation when that is the planned construct.

indications.text: Used for anterior access to C1–C2.

closure.text: Suture platysma, then fat and skin, and place a drain through a separate stab.

complications.text: Complications include esophageal perforation, recurrent-laryngeal palsy, and carotid injury.

procedure_applications.condition: Anterior C1–C2 work is done through the same retropharyngeal plane used for subaxial anterior cervical exposure

questions.question: What is the deep plane to C1–C2 from the front?
questions.answer: Between the carotid sheath and the trachea/esophagus, down to prevertebral fascia.

questions.question: Why place a nasogastric tube?
questions.answer: To identify the esophagus and help prevent accidental injury.
